blocks.text: Condo buildings in London Landing

No City of Richmond source read uses it for any Richmond area. The official name for this ground is London Landing — the City's Zoning Bylaw No. 8500 carries site-specific "London Landing (Steveston)" zones, the City runs London's Wharf Park at the foot of No. 2 Road, and City council material names developments "at London Landing" on London Road and No. 2 Road in Steveston.
The Pier at London Landing — 6160 and 6168 London Road

Strata plan EPS2689, 76 units in total (MLS data sheet for a unit in the building), managed by FirstService Residential (same data sheet). Built 2016 per current listings, which record frame-wood construction, geothermal heating and cooling, air conditioning, an elevator, bike room and in-suite laundry, with marina and river views. Published restrictions: current listings state rentals and pets allowed; the building's MLS data sheet records 2 pets, cats and dogs yes. A published age restriction: UNCONFIRMED.
Harbour Walk — 13040 No. 2 Road

The mixed-use building on the site the City rezoned to the site-specific "Commercial Mixed Use (ZMU24) – London Landing (Steveston)" zone (Bylaw 9094, public hearing May 20, 2014) for a four-storey building with approximately 55 residential units and about 348.5 m² of commercial space. Built 2021 per current listings. The building carries both forms at one address: apartment/condo units (a current listing records a 1-bedroom apartment unit with 9-foot ceilings, clubhouse and exercise centre among the amenities) and townhouse-form units (a current listing records a 2-level townhouse unit with a private fenced yard, the strata fee including city utilities). Published restrictions for the apartment component: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Nautica South — 12639 No. 2 Road

A low-rise apartment building in Steveston South, just north of the London Landing No. 2 Road strip (the pocket's rezoning addresses begin at 12771 No. 2 Road). Built 1998 per current listings, which name the building Nautica South and describe waterfront setting with direct access to the Steveston Boardwalk and the West and South Dyke trail systems, marina and Fraser River views, and a gas fireplace in units. Published restrictions: current listing data records pets "Cats OK"; a verified rental or age position is UNCONFIRMED.
Nautica North — 12633 No. 2 Road

The companion building immediately beside Nautica South, at the same flagged edge position. Built 1997 per current listings, which name the building Nautica North and record an elevator and wheelchair access, in-suite laundry, and marina, recreation and shopping among the area amenities. Unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.

items.t: London Landing is the waterfront pocket at the east edge of Steveston, at the south foot of No. 2 Road where London Road and Dyke Road meet the South Arm of the Fraser River. It sits inside the Steveston planning area under the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan); in board listing practice this ground falls inside Steveston South. No City source read publishes a boundary for a "London Landing" neighbourhood — the sourced anchors are London's Wharf Park at 6062 Dyke Road, London Road (The Pier at London Landing, 6160 London Road), Princess Street (London Landing townhouses, 13200 Princess Street) and the No. 2 Road addresses 12771–13131 now in rezoning.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two clusters. On London Road at the wharf, The Pier at London Landing (6160/6168 London Road) stands over the dyke beside London's Wharf Park, with townhouse stock behind it on London Road and Princess Street/Princess Lane. On No. 2 Road, Harbour Walk (13040 No. 2 Road) carries the pocket's second apartment building. Just north of the pocket's No. 2 Road strip, across Steveston Highway, the older Nautica North and Nautica South buildings (12633/12639 No.

The waterfront anchor: London's Wharf Park, 6062 Dyke Road, is just under 4 acres, with the No. 2 Road Pier, expansive river views, trail connections to the South Arm Dyke and Steveston Greenways trail networks, a playground, benches, open lawn and a public restroom at the north end of the pier; the City ran a 2026 "Have Your Say" process on recent changes and future improvements at the park. The City's Steveston Greenways material describes London's Landing / No. 2 Road Fishing Pier as a historic area starting at the South Dyke Trail, with views of Steveston Island (Shady Island) and the historic Cannery Channel.

Village services: Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, holds the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex for the district, and Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) is at 4320 Moncton Street; village shops, markets and services centre on Moncton Street in Steveston Village to the west. The nearest hospital is Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway. Transit: buses serve Steveston Exchange on Chatham Street, including TransLink route 401 (One Road) to Richmond–Brighouse Station via No. 1 Road; a route stopping inside London Landing itself is UNVERIFIED. Main roads: No. 2 Road, London Road, Dyke Road, Steveston Highway.

items.t: City plans and zoning — the pocket's own zones: London Landing sits inside the Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4 of the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 9000). Zoning is Richmond Zoning Bylaw No. 8500: Section 20.20 is the site-specific "Commercial Mixed Use (ZMU20) – London Landing (Steveston)" zone, created by Bylaw 8818 (September 24, 2012), providing for commercial, residential and industrial uses with a maximum floor area ratio of 1.2 plus 0.1, maximum lot coverage of 76% and maximum height of 21.0 m; the ZMU24 zone at 13040 No. 2 Road was created by Bylaw 9094 in 2014. In July 2026 City staff reported an application to redesignate No. 2 Road lands here from "Industrial" to "Local Village – Tier 1" in the Steveston Waterfront Neighbourhood Land Use Map.

The live rezoning on No. 2 Road: on July 8, 2026, City staff reported application RZ 25-009451 by Jim Pattison Developments to rezone 13131, 13111, 13031, 12931 and 12771 No. 2 Road from Light Industrial (IL) to a new "Residential / Limited Commercial (ZMU63) – London Landing (Steveston)" zone, with OCP Amendment Bylaw 10771 and Zoning Amendment Bylaw 10772, to permit a five- and six-storey residential and commercial mixed-use project — an application in process, not an approval. 2 Road purchase.

Heritage: the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area sits at the district's south-west waterfront west of this pocket, and properties inside it are subject to Heritage Alteration Permit requirements under the Steveston Area Plan; whether any London Landing parcel sits inside the conservation area boundary is UNVERIFIED.

items.t: "Lower Landing" appears in no City source read; "London Landing (Steveston)" is written into Zoning Bylaw No. 8500 itself (ZMU20 at Section 20.20, Bylaw 8818, 2012; ZMU24 at Bylaw 9094, 2014; a proposed ZMU63 in 2026). Searches, contracts and strata documents for this pocket run under London Landing and Steveston South — a buyer searching "Lower Landing" will miss the record.

The Pier's strata paperwork is unusually well pinned down. Its MLS data sheet records strata plan EPS2689, 76 units total, FirstService Residential as manager, and 2 pets (cats and dogs yes) — the four facts buyers usually have to order documents to learn, all published for this building.

Harbour Walk's 2021 building is bigger in form than its 2014 paper. The ZMU24 rezoning described approximately 55 residential units over about 348.5 m² of commercial space; the finished building sells both apartment units and townhouse-form units at the single 13040 No. 2 Road address, with strata fees that at least one listing states include city utilities.

The industrial strip beside the condos is mid-conversion. The five No. 2 Road lots in RZ 25-009451 (12771–13131) are Light Industrial today; the same July 2026 staff process also carries an OCP redesignation of No.

The wharf park is an active City project, not a finished fact. London's Wharf Park (6062 Dyke Road, just under 4 acres, No. 2 Road Pier) went through a City "Have Your Say" process in 2026 on recent changes and future improvements — the waterfront at The Pier's front door is still being decided.

Commercial strata lots hide inside the same streetscape. The retail units at 6033 London Road (zoned ZMU14) trade on commercial listings, not residential ones — a "London Landing strata unit" can be a shop, an office, a townhouse or a condo, and only the zoning and strata plan say which.

London Station — 6111 London Road. STRATA

A listing records Sub-Type Row / Townhouse (also shown as Townhouse), built 2007, a 3-bedroom townhome of about 1,492 sq ft filed under Steveston South, with strata-structure amenities including 2 secured underground parking stalls, EV charging, a large storage locker, caretaker/management-type services; developer-era marketing in the Richmond Review (April 2007) sold the project as "condominium residences at London Station" — condominium form, i.e., strata.
Princess Lane at London Landing — 6431 Princess Lane. STRATA

The building directory's page for the complex records built 2005 with strata restrictions recorded as "Pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental-restriction element of that line is VOID for long-term rentals since Nov 24, 2022; the pets element is a bylaw question for the Form B. A second directory page under the same complex name at 6333 Princess Lane records built 2003 — treated here as ONE complex with an address/year spread flagged (6431 Princess Lane / built 2005 on the page followed; 6333 Princess Lane / built 2003 on the second page), not as two complexes. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Currents — 6451 Princess Lane. STRATA

Building data records built 2011, 18 homes in 2 storeys, frame-wood construction, Title Freehold Strata, strata plan BCP41008, managed by River West Property Management — a low-rise strata in the Princess Lane cluster, carried here as townhouse-form stock on its 2-storey, lane-cluster form; if a specific unit's built form is apartment-style, its diligence is the same strata diligence either way.
London Landing townhouses — 13200 Princess Street

City of Richmond council material from 2002 documents a townhouse development by London Landing Development Corp. in the London Landing area at Steveston's east edge — the development is City-documented, but its tenure (strata vs fee-simple), exact year and unit count are UNCONFIRMED in the sources read, so it is documented here and deliberately NOT folded into the verified count. The neighbouring Princess Lane / Currents entries above are separate, later strata product and are not assumed to be this development.

In the ZMU mixed-use buildings, read the depreciation report, contingency fund and commercial-component cost sharing early — these are mixed-use strata, not pure residential ones. blocks.text: Good to know about London Landing

items.t: The name is a family, not a direction. In 1881 brothers Charles and William London bought 200 acres at the south end of No. 2 Road at what became known as London's Landing — every official use since (the ZMU zones, the wharf park, the buildings) descends from that family name, which is why "Lower Landing" finds nothing in any City source.

The fishing pier is a historic working site, not just a viewpoint: the City's Steveston Greenways material describes London's Landing / No. 2 Road Fishing Pier as a historic area starting at the South Dyke Trail, with views of Steveston Island (Shady Island) and the historic Cannery Channel, and a fishing float, picnic tables, washrooms, interpretation signage and parking.

The pocket's zoning is site-specific, street by street: ZMU20 was written for London Landing in 2012 (Bylaw 8818) and ZMU24 for one No. 2 Road site in 2014 (Bylaw 9094) — there is no general "London Landing zone" to quote; each building's permissions live in its own section of Bylaw 8500.

The district's civic anchor is west in the village: Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, holds the Steveston Community Centre, pool and library complex, and Richmond Public Library's Steveston Branch (Easthope Hub) is at 4320 Moncton Street — London Landing residents use village facilities, not in-pocket ones.
The nearest hospital is across Richmond: Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway (Vancouver Coastal Health) — a London Landing buyer's hospital is a cross-city trip, not a Steveston one.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in London Landing

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw 8500, site-specific London Landing zones: Section 20.20 is the site-specific "Commercial Mixed Use (ZMU20) – London Landing (Steveston)" zone, created by Bylaw 8818 (September 24, 2012), providing for commercial, residential and industrial uses in the Steveston area, with maximum FAR 1.2 plus 0.1, maximum lot coverage 76% and maximum height 21.0 m. ZMU24 (13040 No. 2 Road, Bylaw 9094, 2014) is the pocket's second site-specific zone. Edge houses sit in RS1/RS2 (Section 8.1).

OCP — Official Community Plan Bylaw 9000 / Steveston Area Plan (Schedule 2.4): London Landing sits inside the Steveston planning area under Schedule 2.4 of the OCP. Whether any London Landing parcel sits inside the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area boundary (Heritage Alteration Permit requirements): UNVERIFIED.

Flood Control — Bylaw 8204: new construction is subject to flood construction levels and dike setbacks under the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 — for waterfront and dyke-adjacent lots in this pocket, confirm both before pricing in a rebuild or addition.

Strata diligence in the ZMU buildings (the pocket's core tenure): these are mixed-use strata — read the Form B, depreciation report, contingency fund and commercial-component cost sharing early. The full BC strata block applies: Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no pocket ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.
